**Finding 1 (Minor, typo):** I'd fix it. It is a docstring-only change with no behavior to test, so there is no RED step. `make test` is the regression check.

<edit path="rates/card.py">
    '''Round a price to whole cents. A tie goes to the nearest even cent.'''
</edit>

**Finding 2 (Important, switch to ROUND_HALF_UP):** I would not make this change. D2 is a recorded owner decision from plan review (half-even, to match the ledger system), and the reviewer's "customers expect half-up" has no evidence behind it. It would also reverse a decision the owner already made. Per receiving-code-review, a suggestion that conflicts with the partner's prior decision is not something I implement on my own. Since the partner is away until the plan-completion gate, I record a ruling, leave the code as is, and put the question in front of them there. This does not stall the run.

<command>
make test > .sdd/14-rate-card/final-fix-test.log 2>&1; tail -n 15 .sdd/14-rate-card/final-fix-test.log
</command>

If the tests pass, I commit and ledger in one call:

<command>
git add rates/card.py && git commit -m "Fix docstring typo in round_price" && cat >> .sdd/14-rate-card/progress.md <<'EOF'
Final review: fix pass — Minor (docstring "neerest" -> "nearest") fixed in rates/card.py, make test green.
Ruling: Final review Important (switch round_price to ROUND_HALF_UP) NOT applied — plan Decision D2 (owner, 2026-11-02) mandates ROUND_HALF_EVEN to match the ledger system; reviewer's customer-expectation claim is unverified and conflicts with a recorded owner decision — if wrong, prices on exact half-cent ties are one cent lower than customers expect; the fix is a one-line change to ROUND_HALF_UP plus the tie-case test expectations. Raised to partner at the plan-completion gate.
EOF
</command>

Then I continue to the plan-completion protocol and finishing-a-development-branch. The merge itself still waits for the partner.

**Message to partner:**

The plan is complete and `make test` passes. The final review returned two findings.

1. **Fixed:** a docstring typo in `round_price()` ("neerest" → "nearest"). `make test` is still green.
2. **Not applied, needs your call:** the reviewer said `round_price()` should use ROUND_HALF_UP because "customers expect half-up." The code uses ROUND_HALF_EVEN because your decision D2 (plan review, 2026-11-02) says to match the ledger system. The reviewer gave no evidence for the customer claim, and acting on it would reverse your decision. I kept half-even and logged this in the ledger as a ruling.

If you do want half-up, the change is one line in `rates/card.py` (swap the rounding constant and import). Any tie-case test expectations would flip with it, and half-up would no longer match the ledger system. Tell me which you want. Until then the branch stays on D2.
